chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Assistance descends upon a people according to their needs, and indeed the guest lodges with a people so his sustenance descends with him in his lap.

key_terms.الْقَوْمِ: The people or a specific group
key_terms.الْمَعُونَةُ: Assistance or help provided by God or people
key_terms.حَجْرِهِ: His lap or domain (indicating proximity and inclusion)
key_terms.مَئُونَتِهِمْ: Their needs, expenses, or cost of living

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between a guest's arrival and their sustenance in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes a spiritual economy where divine sustenance (rizq) is proportional to one's capacity and need, illustrated by the guest who brings his own provision. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on hospitality as a means of unlocking hidden blessings, linking the physical act of hosting with the metaphysical reality that the guest's rizq descends alongside them. It serves as a practical reminder that generosity is not merely a social duty but a mechanism for attracting divine grace.
